ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$, $\angle B=\angle D=90^\circ$, $CB=CD$, $\angle 1=30^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $\angle B=\angle D=90^\circ$\\
Therefore, both $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$ are right-angled triangles. \\
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$: \\
Since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}CB=CD\\ AC=AC\end{array}\right.$\\
Therefore, $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle ADC$ (HL criterion)\\
Therefore, $\angle 1 = \angle CAD$\\
Since $\angle 2 + \angle CAD + \angle D = 180^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle 2 = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 30^\circ = \boxed{60^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point C is on the left side, point A is on the right side, point B is on the upper left, and point D is on the lower left; segment AC is the common side of the upper triangle ABC and the lower triangle ADC. In the figure, angle 1 of the upper triangle is marked at point A, namely ∠BAC; angle 2 of the lower triangle is marked at point C, namely ∠ACD. The problem gives ∠B=∠D=90°, CB=CD, and ∠1=30°. Reasoning: Because ∠B=90°, △ABC is a right triangle, and AC is its hypotenuse; because ∠D=90°, △ADC is a right triangle, and AC is also its hypotenuse. In the two right triangles, AC is the common hypotenuse, and CB=CD is a pair of corresponding right-angle sides, so by the HL criterion, △ABC≅△ADC. Thus the corresponding angles are equal, ∠BAC=∠CAD. Also ∠1=∠BAC=30°, so ∠CAD=30°. In △ADC, ∠D=90°, therefore ∠2=∠ACD=180°−90°−30°=60°.
